input: # A quoted field holds every character but an unescaped quote. A TAB, an
# ASCII 30 (RS), an ASCII 31 (US) or any other control character between
# the quotes is field text, as Go's encoding/csv, Python's csv module and
# Papa Parse read it, and as the CSV renderer writes it, because CSV has no
# other spelling for such a cell (tabnas/csv#82). The fixture codec decodes
# only the escapes for TAB, LF, CR and backslash, so some input cells below
# hold raw RS, US and DEL bytes. NUL has a file of its own.
# TAB, RS and US inside a quoted field.
# DEL was never refused; it is pinned beside the rest.
# At either end of the field, alone, several together, in the header row,
# and in more than one field of a record.
# Beside a doubled quote and a line break, which keep their meaning.
# A quoted field still has to close.
# The same under a custom quote, for a quote character the CSV matcher does
# not own, under the escape option (string.csv false, so a backslash
# escapes), and in non-strict mode with either matcher.
# A quote that is itself a control character still opens and closes the
# field, and a doubled one is a literal quote.
# A line break is still refused inside a jsonic string, whose single and
# double quoted forms hold one line.
# A control character that is also the field separator: a quoted field
# holds it, as it holds a comma under the default separator.
# Under custom record separators, LF is not a line character, so a quoted
# field holds it as it holds any other control character.
# An unquoted field reads a control character as text, as it always has.
# What the CSV renderer writes for four documents of test/fixtures read
# under the default comma (every field quoted, a doubled quote, records
# ending in CRLF), each reading back to the value the document reads to.
